name: Terrain Tile Source Nodes
description: The PURE half of the terrain serving lane: it decodes source DEM GeoTIFF granules into quantized-mesh-1.0 tiles wrapped in $DTT records, and renders the tileset's layer.json, and does nothing else. capabilities [], browser + wasmedge, request-scoped, no state between invocations. Every DEM byte it decodes was fetched by com.digitalarsenal.hostcap.http-request and every record it emits is persisted downstream; scheduling and pyramid orchestration live in the sibling terrain-ingest module, exactly as geonames-source / geonames-ingest are split. The source granules are DEFLATE-compressed Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs and there is no host inflate capability (and none may be added), so miniz 3.1.2 is vendored under vendor/miniz-3.1.2 (MIT, SHA-256 pinned and re-verified on every build) - the same vendored copy geonames-source and cell-tower-source use. A minimal little-endian TIFF/BigTIFF reader (tiled or strip layout, DEFLATE via tinfl, predictor 1 and floating-point predictor 3) lives in-guest for the same reason. Heights are redistributed on the source dataset's own vertical datum (a geoid), stated verbatim in VERTICAL_DATUM/VERTICAL_DATUM_NAME, never silently converted.

sequentialJustification.detail: Both methods are single-pass transforms over the frames the flow hands them: decode the DEM granules covering one output tile and encode one quantized mesh, or render one layer.json body. Tiles are processed one at a time, there is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest, so it compiles single-thread rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

acceptedTypeSets.description: hostcap/http-request responses carrying the source DEM GeoTIFF granules intersecting the plan's union extent, over responseWire "raw-body-v1" ($HRB: magic, little-endian status, body verbatim). The default JSON/bodyB64 dialect is still read so a recorded fixture stays replayable. A 404 is a granule the dataset does not publish (open ocean), which is data, not an error.

wildcardJustification.detail: Intra-flow connector frame produced and consumed inside this flow: hostcap/http-request's responseWire "raw-body-v1" $HRB frame (magic, little-endian status, body verbatim) carrying one DEFLATE-compressed Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF elevation granule, or the same response in the connector's default JSON/bodyB64 dialect. The frame's shape is defined by that host op and the body by the source dataset, neither by SDS.

inputPorts.description: One response frame per source elevation granule intersecting the plan's union extent; an extent straddling a 2x2 granule neighbourhood needs four.

acceptedTypeSets.description: hostcap/http-request responses carrying the source WATER-BODY granules covering the same extent, over responseWire "raw-body-v1" ($HRB). Single-band 8-bit categorical rasters: 0 is no water, any non-zero class is a water body. Sampled NEAREST-NEIGHBOUR - a land/water class is never interpolated, because averaging class ordinals invents a class the source never stated. Absent (404) leaves the tile on the plan's directive.

The frame's shape is defined by that host op and the body by the source dataset, neither by SDS.

methods.description: Decodes the source granules covering the plan's extent and encodes quantized-mesh-1.0 tiles of the GEOGRAPHIC_WGS84 pyramid (two root tiles, TMS row origin south): ECEF header with bounding sphere and horizon occlusion point, zigzag-delta 16-bit vertex arrays, high-water-mark index encoding, edge index lists, and the watermask extension (id 2). AMORTIZED: a plan may address ONE tile or a tiles[] BLOCK, and a block decodes its granule set ONCE over the union extent and emits every tile the set covers - the per-tile re-decode it replaces spent about 97% of its time inflating the same bytes again. WINDOWED: only the internal chunks intersecting the extent are inflated, so resident memory is proportional to the OUTPUT, not to the granule; a named 256 MiB in-guest decode budget is checked before every raster allocation and against the running total across granules, refusing with "decode-budget-exceeded" rather than trapping a pooled flow instance. WATER MASK: classified from the water-body granules on ONE GLOBAL POST LATTICE per level, so the posts two adjacent tiles share are the same global posts and their bytes are equal by construction; 256x256 at every level, row 0 the NORTH edge, 255 water and 0 land, reduced to a single uniform byte where the whole tile agrees. WATER_MASK is set together with its width and height, and carries WATER_MASK_PROVENANCE when the mask's licence differs from the elevation dataset's. The tile bytes ride INLINE in DTTPayloadRef.BYTES (gzip via the vendored deflate, CONTENT_ENCODING "gzip"); SIZE_BYTES and DIGEST are stated over those GZIPPED bytes and the record's ETAG is that digest, so a cache revalidates against the bytes it actually holds. A tile past the 32 KiB gzipped per-tile serving ceiling is REFUSED at encode time. HEIGHTS ARE NOT CONVERTED: the source dataset publishes geoid-referenced heights and the record states VERTICAL_DATUM GEOID with the model named verbatim - a consumer that renders them as ellipsoidal accepts a stated, bounded error and the record and report both say so. A granule the dataset does not publish (HTTP 404, open ocean) decodes to height 0 with WATER_MASK_KIND UNIFORM_WATER unless the plan states otherwise; the source NO_DATA value (-32767) decodes to 0 and is counted in DATA_COVERAGE_FRACTION rather than hidden. A plan that cannot state the dataset identity, epoch, retrieval time and licence is REFUSED, never defaulted. BATCHING: the plan port is single-stream and the dem and water ports carry at most four frames each, ENFORCED IN CODE; maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely declarative in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind, so any surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames" rather than silently destroyed.

methods.description: SERVING LANE (flows/terrain-serving.flow.json, mount /api/v1/terrain/): renders the complete layer.json body for a quantized-mesh-1.0 tileset - tilejson 2.1.0, format quantized-mesh-1.0, scheme tms, projection EPSG:4326, bounds [-180,-90,180,90], minzoom 0, the plan's maxzoom, extensions ["watermask"] (octvertexnormals is omitted until normals ship), and the plan's available ranges passed through VERBATIM - and emits it as the SDK's canonical $HTR HttpResponse envelope with the body inline, never as a JSON control frame. The availability index is the orchestrator's knowledge, not this encoder's, so it is never synthesized here. BATCHING: single-stream by contract, enforced in code; a surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames".

methods.description: One $HTQ in, exactly ONE downstream path out. The mount prefix is config-owned (the node mounts this flow at /api/v1/terrain/, sdn-server lane), so the router strips up to and including the LAST "/terrain/" segment. "layer.json" => a layer_plan frame for the sibling layer_json node, composed from plugin.getConfig keys terrain_tileset_id / terrain_maxzoom / terrain_available (VERBATIM availability array; defaults to the two level-0 roots, honest exactly when maxzoom is 0 - a deeper pyramid MUST configure terrain_available; the per-request SQL-aggregate availability upgrade is recorded here, not silently skipped) / terrain_attribution / terrain_description / terrain_version. "{z}/{x}/{y}.terrain" => a {sql,params} frame for hostcap/flatsql-query:query (SELECT _data FROM DTT WHERE TILESET_ID/LEVEL/X/Y, ORDER BY rowid DESC LIMIT 1) plus a context frame carrying the address and the client's If-None-Match. Anything else => a direct, CACHEABLE $HTR 404 (public, max-age=300) because a miss is normal traffic, and 405 for non-GET/HEAD. plugin.getConfig is the module's only hostcall - reading who it was deployed as, the geonames-ingest precedent, not a capability. BATCHING: single-stream by contract, enforced in code; a surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames".

methods.description: Walks the aligned size-prefixed $DTT stream (zero-length prefixes are alignment padding; size-prefixed verify first, plain-anchored fallback - the foundation/omm-json framing contract) and serves the FIRST record: 200 with the payload BYTES VERBATIM (they are already gzip-compressed at encode time), content-type and content-encoding FROM THE RECORD (never re-negotiated), cache-control public max-age=86400, and a strong ETag (record ETAG verbatim, else the payload DIGEST quoted, else a weak address+size tag). An If-None-Match match answers 304 with no body. An EMPTY stream answers a cheap CACHEABLE 404 (public, max-age=300) - an unpublished tile is normal traffic, the client's upsampling relies on layer.json availability, and a 404 must never be an error. A record whose payload is CID-only (no inline BYTES) is REFUSED loudly rather than served as an empty body that would render as fabricated sea-level terrain - the CID resolution lane is the recorded growth path. BATCHING: single-stream by contract, enforced in code; a surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames".
